canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across papers, the prevailing usage treats logical consistency as internal non-contradiction: outputs, summaries, dialogues, or reasoning chains are described as logically structured, coherent, and free of discrepancies. A smaller line of work defines it more narrowly as whether responses to logically related inputs obey logic, for example when a statement and its negation receive semantically opposite answers, when conclusions follow from premises, or when decisions remain invariant across equivalent formulations. Other task-specific definitions shift the reference point from text alone to predictions on decomposed NLI sub-problems, beliefs over related claims, adherence of generated programs to domain knowledge, or similarity between agent and human operational logic.

Space of facets. Most papers use nearby labels for closely similar ideas, especially logical coherence and logical robustness, and a few rename the same theme as solution consistency or reasoning coherence. One evaluation framework places logical robustness inside a broader logical thinking category alongside logical correctness and logical efficiency, while a narrower variant, logical plausibility, targets whether a sub-query is consistent with the prior reasoning context. The same label is also used at different units of analysis, from plot and theme consistency in summaries to chain-of-thought steps, sub-problem predictions, belief trees, generated programs, and application-switching behavior.

Space of measurement. Papers link the construct to 4 measurement instruments and 4 behavioral indicators. The linked instruments cover model-based evaluation, direct judging, and dataset-based checks: FLASK is used through its logical thinking category, including logical correctness, logical robustness, and logical efficiency; human evaluation asks annotators to choose the most logical rationale; LLM-as-a-judge uses DeepSeek R1 and ERNIE Bot 4.0 to score outputs for logical consistency, clarity, and lack of ambiguity; and SNLI operationalizes it as consistency between original instances and their sub-problems. These operationalizations mostly match the dominant non-contradiction framing, though the SNLI setup narrows it to agreement under logically necessary constraints rather than general output quality.

Links. Several papers connect logical consistency to neighboring reasoning constructs and application settings. It is related to logical reasoning, and papers also relate it to fact-checking and to improving consistency with domain knowledge in generated programs. Papers claim a causal relationship from logical consistency to hallucination and to factuality, though some phrasing is looser: one paper says a logically consistent LLM is less likely to hallucinate, another says hallucination stems from optimizing for likelihood rather than truth or logical consistency, and another says factuality can be improved using consistency across beliefs while a separate paper calls factuality and consistency intimately related. In the reverse direction, one survey claims a causal relationship from self-reflection to logical consistency, and no correlational link is reported.

relationships.paper: FLASK: Fine-grained Language Model Evaluation based on Alignment Skill Sets
relationships.evidence: We define 4 primary abilities which are divided into 12 fine-grained skills for comprehensive language model evaluation: Logical Thinking (Logical Correctness, Logical Robustness, Logical Efficiency)... (Section 1)

iclr24: FLASK: Fine-grained Language Model Evaluation based on Alignment Skill Sets

relationships.paper: Logical Consistency of Large Language Models in Fact-Checking
relationships.evidence: A logically consistent LLM is less likely to hallucinate since its response is unlikely to change due to the logical manipulation of the prompt.

iclr25: Logical Consistency of Large Language Models in Fact-Checking
icml25: Position: Trustworthy AI Agents Require the Integration of Large Language Models and Formal Methods

relationships.paper: A Probabilistic Framework for LLM Hallucination Detection via Belief Tree Propagation
relationships.evidence: A growing body of research explores improving LLMs’ factuality using the logical consistency across their beliefs (Dalvi et al., 2021; Tafjord et al., 2022; Mitchell et al., 2022; Jung et al., 2022; Hase et al., 2023; Kassner et al., 2023; Akyürek et al., 2024).

iclr25: Logically Consistent Language Models via Neuro-Symbolic Integration

relationships.evidence: "For human evaluation, 100 questions were sampled from each dataset, with annotators selecting the most logical rationale among those generated by ToT, GoT, and our method"

neurips24: Decompose, Analyze and Rethink: Solving Intricate Problems with Human-like Reasoning Cycle

relationships.paper: Theorem-Validated Reverse Chain-of-Thought Problem Generation for Geometric Reasoning
relationships.evidence: We use DeepSeek R1 and ERNIE Bot 4.0 to quantitatively evaluate model outputs before and after training, focusing on logical consistency, clarity, and lack of ambiguity (Section 5)

emnlp25: Theorem-Validated Reverse Chain-of-Thought Problem Generation for Geometric Reasoning

relationships.paper: NLI under the Microscope: What Atomic Hypothesis Decomposition Reveals
relationships.evidence: we evaluate their logical consistency between each original SNLI instance and its corresponding sub-problems.

naacl25: NLI under the Microscope: What Atomic Hypothesis Decomposition Reveals

relationships.paper: Towards Rationality in Language and Multimodal Agents: A Survey
relationships.evidence: Multi-round self-reflection that encourages a single LLM to critically evaluate its previous responses has demonstrated the effectiveness of deliberation in improving logical coherence and qualities (Section 4.2.1)

naacl25: Towards Rationality in Language and Multimodal Agents: A Survey

relationships.paper: Self-Training Meets Consistency: Improving LLMs' Reasoning with Consistency-Driven Rationale Evaluation
relationships.evidence: we employ FLASK (Ye et al., 2024), a fine-grained evaluation protocol for model-based evaluation, which exhibits a high correlation with human-based evaluation. Specifically, we focus on the ‘logical thinking’ category in FLASK, which encompasses three aspects: logical correctness, logical robustness, and logical efficiency.

naacl25: Self-Training Meets Consistency: Improving LLMs' Reasoning with Consistency-Driven Rationale Evaluation

relationships.paper: Logical Consistency of Large Language Models in Fact-Checking
relationships.evidence: "We assess and improve the logical consistency of LLMs in propositional logic queries and logic rules, particularly in the context of fact-checking."

iclr25: Logical Consistency of Large Language Models in Fact-Checking

relationships.paper: Learning to Solve Domain-Specific Calculation Problems with Knowledge-Intensive Programs Generator
relationships.evidence: By iterative preference alignment, the code generator learns to improve the logic consistency with the domain knowledge. (Abstract)
